# ICMA Exercise (last class): two variables

Using the `mpg` dataset plot a frequency polygon of the `hwy` variable, with the `class` variable mapped to the color aesthetic

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = hwy)) + 
  geom_freqpoly(aes(color = class), binwidth = 2,linewidth = 1)
```

# ICMA Exercise (last class): histograms vs. boxplots

Below I have plotted a histograms and boxplots of the same data. Both plots show the variation of the `carat` variable from the `diamonds` data set.

Compare and contrast the two plots. What kind of information is highlighted by each? What kind of information is highlighted by both?



```{r}
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = carat)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1)
```

```{r}
diamonds |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = carat)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = 'red')
```

In the bloxplot, it clearly shows the outliers that are in the graph. The histogram also shows us a clearer distributional shape for the data. 


# Slide 24

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = class)) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Engine displacement (L)",
    y = "Highway fuel economy (mpg)",
    color = "Car type",
    title = "Fuel efficiency generally decreases with engine size",
    subtitle = "Two seaters (sports cars) are an exception because of their light weight",
    caption = "Data from fueleconomy.gov"
  )
```

# Slide 26

```{r}
df <- tribble(~y, ~x, ~label,
        1, 1, "point")
df |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = y, x = x)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label))
```

# Slide 30

```{r}

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  annotate(
    geom = "label", x = 3.5, y = 38,
    label = str_wrap("Larger engine sizes tend to have lower fuel economy.", 
           width = 30),
    hjust = "left", color = "red"
  ) +
  annotate(
    geom = "segment",
    x = 3, y = 35, xend = 5, yend = 25, color = "red",
    arrow = arrow(type = "closed")
  )
```


# Slide 33
```{r}

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = drv)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(15, 40, by = 5)) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = c("4" = "4-wheel", "f" = "front", "r" = "rear"))

```


# Slide 35

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = drv)) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1")
```

# Slide 38

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = drv)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  annotate(geom = "rect", xmin = 5, xmax = 6, ymin = 10, ymax = 30,
           fill = "lightgrey", colour = "black", alpha = 0.5)
```

# Slide 40

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = drv)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(5, 6), ylim = c(10, 25))
```

# Slide 42

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = class)) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() # using theme_bw() with no additional modifications
```
